body: `fulfillOrder` currently accepts any amount that does not exactly match a configured plan and falls back to granting access based on a threshold. Because this service is now used by both direct verification and webhooks, an unexpected Razorpay order amount (including a non-upgrade order at the upgrade price) should fail closed instead of granting Lite/Pro access.

The new admin toggle writes `telemetry_enabled`, but this notification route never reads that setting, so lock-modal telemetry is still sent even when an admin disables it. Check `getTelemetryEnabled()` before sending the Telegram event so the toggle actually controls these logs.

This is a public, unauthenticated endpoint that forwards each valid request to Telegram, but it has no server-side rate limit. The client-side `sessionStorage` throttle can be bypassed by calling the API directly, which could spam the Telegram channel and consume outbound resources.

`userEmail` is interpolated into a Telegram HTML message without escaping, while the rest of the user-provided fields in this message are escaped. A malformed email value containing HTML metacharacters can break `parse_mode: 'HTML'` or inject formatting into the admin notification.

The schema now adds `system_settings`, and the admin telemetry toggle reads/writes it, but this manual migration only creates `intelligence_feedback`. Deployments that use this script will still fail the telemetry actions with `no such table: system_settings`. Add the `system_settings` DDL here as well.

body: This unique index does not reliably prevent duplicate submissions: `startTime` is derived from `Date.now() - validDuration`, so two concurrent submissions for the same user/test will usually have different timestamps and both satisfy this constraint. Use a deterministic idempotency key or a partial unique constraint on the fields that define a duplicate attempt instead.

This reads `APP_guest_name`, but the quiz flow stores guest names under `mppolice_guest_name`; it also sends that value as `guestMobile`, so guest feedback is saved in the mobile column instead of the name column. Use the existing guest-name key for `userName` and only send `guestMobile` when an actual mobile value is available.

This repeats the guest identity mix-up from the quick reaction path: `APP_guest_name` is not the key used by the quiz flow, and the retrieved name is sent as `guestMobile`. Comment feedback from guests will therefore lose the guest name and may populate `user_mobile` with a name string.

The rest of the quiz flow stores the guest name in `mppolice_guest_name` (for example `GuestQuizInterface` and `QuizResult`), so this new telemetry helper will not include guest names for existing guests. Read the established key instead of `APP_guest_name`.
